localChanges: 25 packages, 9 waves, all verified live on the registry and pushed with tags. Full re-resolve rather than `pnpm update`, per 04-package-workflow.md: one copy of each of the 328 packages, every installed copy matching its checkout.

Conformance unchanged against the published artifacts: aebaf5c2 / af0ade7e / f6e495ff, 9/9 hydrated, 13/13 isolated, 27/27 transient. The DTO digest — the renderer's actual transport payload — is byte-identical at all three checkpoints (788 / 3,245 / 53,120 objects, 8.9MB at turn 50, hashes 67d92604 / c27f4b32 / 40a7e611), as are the 1,055 rules across 65 types.

log: Stage 4 of the engine serialisation plan. Every field of a `DataObject` is saved unless the class says otherwise, and some of them must not be: a registry, an `Engine`, a random number generator and a cache are either supplied by the loading `Game` or derived from what it supplies, and restoring one restores a stale answer at best.

`static readonly transient` lists them. The set is derived from the field types rather than hand-written — a field typed with a registry class, with a type the `Game` holds, or with `() => number` is transient by construction, and a cache is matched by name because it has no distinguishing type. Stages 2 and 3 were mechanical for the same reason.

The dependency on core-data-object moves to ^0.1.15 because that is the first version the declaration is both read and safe in. Against an older one it is legal TypeScript that compiles to an unread static, so the field would be saved regardless and nothing would report it; 0.1.14 reads it but declared the static as required, which stopped `IConstructor<T>` satisfying `typeof T` and broke the typecheck of 22 of the 83 checkouts.
This changes nothing yet: `stateKeys()` has no callers until the save format lands, and `toPlainObject()` is unaffected, so the conformance checksums and the DTO digest are both unchanged.

0.1.14 declared `static readonly transient: readonly string[]`. A *required* static is the problem: `IConstructor<T>` is `new (...args: any[]) => T` and carries no statics, so it satisfies `typeof T` only while `T` has none that are required.

`ConstructorRegistry<T>` hands out `IConstructor<T>` and the codebase annotates what it gets back as `typeof X`. `core-science/PlayerResearch.available()` and `core-government/PlayerGovernment.available()` both do, and both stopped compiling — taking 22 of the 83 checkouts with them, since a package typechecks its dependencies' source.

Nothing failed in this package either way: its own tests pass, and they still do. That is the whole reason this shipped, so the guard is a compile-time assertion rather than a test — `Assert<IConstructor< DataObject> extends typeof DataObject ? true : false>` fails with TS2344 the moment a required static is added again. Verified by putting the required declaration back and watching it fire.
`allTransient()` already read the member as `transient?: readonly string[]` behind an `Array.isArray` check, so the optional type costs nothing at runtime and the mechanism is unchanged.

The other two items of Stage 4, from 01-constraints.md §9.

`_additionalData` was write-only. `setAdditionalData()` filled it and nothing in any of the 83 checkouts ever read it — the mechanism that makes additional data reachable is the `Object.defineProperty` and `addKey()` on the following lines, not the field. It held a retained copy of every city and unit on the tile, per tile, per player, so deleting it drops that from what `stateKeys()` would save and from what the object keeps alive. `toPlainObject()` never included it, which is why the DTO digest does not move.

`PlayerWorld.entries()` returned `this._tiles` itself. `World.entries()` delegates to `EntityRegistry.entries()` and so has always returned `_entries.slice()`; this now matches. Nothing was mutating the result, so the copy is a guard rather than a fix — but the asymmetry between two methods of the same name and shape is the kind that gets relied on by accident.
Conformance unchanged: 7d6b6b04 / 73a0cc05 / 3431063b.

Against an older one it is legal TypeScript that compiles to an unread static, so the field would be saved regardless and nothing would report it; 0.1.14 reads it but declared the static as required, which stopped `IConstructor<T>` satisfying `typeof T` and broke the typecheck of 22 of the 83 checkouts.
This changes nothing yet: `stateKeys()` has no callers until the save format lands, and `toPlainObject()` is unaffected, so the conformance checksums and the DTO digest are both unchanged.
